goal: Build a simple 3D PDF viewer for Ubuntu that supports mouse-driven rotation of embedded 3D models

items.title: Clarify true embedded-3D (U3D/PRC) vs flat-PDF-in-3D-space
items.notes: User chose true embedded 3D models (U3D/PRC), the harder/CAD-style interpretation

items.title: Research open-source U3D/PRC decoders usable on Linux
items.notes: No usable U3D decoder found (ningfei/u3d encodes IDTF->U3D only). nanoPRC (github.com/mvrhel/nanoPRC, AGPLv3) parses PRC and ships a working SDL3/OpenGL viewer with PDF loading built in.

items.title: Vendor nanoPRC as submodule, build nano_prc_viewer, wrap as 3dpdf-view
items.notes: third_party/nanoPRC pinned @ c6f7c9e. bin/3dpdf-view launcher + scripts/setup.sh + .desktop entry. Verified render (batch mode) and interactive mouse-drag rotation under Xvfb for cube/cylinder/triangle examples.

items.title: Document scope/limitations (no U3D support) and AGPLv3 licensing
Commit and push to GitLab origin
Add middle-mouse-drag pan to the viewer
items.notes: Patched nanoPRC's main.cpp (patches/0001-middle-mouse-pan.patch, applied by setup.sh on top of pinned upstream commit -- submodule itself stays unmodified upstream to keep .gitmodules free of internal URLs). Verified via simulated mouse drag under Xvfb (screenshots/04-panned-cylinder.png).

items.title: Investigate user-reported misplaced components in multi-part assembly PDFs
items.notes: Reproduced with user's enclosure.pdf. Root-caused to nanoPRC's PRC 'prototype' occurrence transform composition: for at least one part, the final placement equals exactly 2x a single transform application (occurrence's own transform and its resolved prototype's own transform were byte-identical, both composed). Unclear if this is a nanoPRC composition bug or an authoring bug in whatever generated enclosure.pdf -- no Adobe Acrobat ground truth or PRC-spec expertise available to disambiguate. Documented in README.md 'Known issue' section. Blocked pending user input on how the PDF was generated, or a decision to attempt a speculative fix without a regression corpus (only 3 simple non-assembly example PDFs available to test against).
